3. That the appellants, as plaintiffs, instituted Other Suit No. 53 of 1987 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chakaria, Cox's Bazar, seeking declaration that the agreement for solenama dated 18.05.1983 is illegal, fraudulent, collusive, inoperative, void and being not acted upon, the plaintiffs' title in the suit land has not been affected by the said solenama and the plaintiffs also sought permanent injunction. It is stated that the land as described in Schedule-1(Ka) to the plaint was sold in auction pursuant to Certificate Case No. 1363 of 1964-65 to the defendant No.1 on the basis of which sale certificate was issued in his favour 4nd accordingly delivery of possession of the same was made on 23.02.1966. It is stated that the predecessor in interest of the defendants No. 2 to 8 filed a case for setting aside the sale and ultimately succeeded to obtain an order in their favour from the Board of Revenue on the basis of which they made an attempt to cause breach of peace and as such the defendant No.1 instituted M.R. Case No. 117 of 1967 under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which ended in terms of compromise admitting the title and possession of the defendant No. 1. Accordingly, the defendant No.1 withdrew the money which was kept with the Receiver in the said "proceeding. They also executed a Nadabi Patra in favour of the defendant No.1 on 06.08.1969. Thereafter, when the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants No. 2 to 8 again made an attempt to create disturbance, the defendant No.1, Abul Kalam, as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 108 of 1972 in the Court of the learned Munsif, Cox's Bazar. The predecessor-in-interest of the defendants No. 2 to 8 appeared in the said suit and filed written statement. Ultimately the said suit No. 108 of 1972 was decreed on con-test and the order of the Board of Revenue was set aside along with a decree for permanent injunction. Thereafter, the defendant No.1 got his name mutated and has been paying rents to the Government. 

 4. The predecessor-in-interest of the def6ndant No. 2 to 8 preferred Other Appeal No. 1 of 1976 against the said decree passed in Other Suit No. 108 of 41972 which was dismissed: Thereafter, they preferred Second Appeal No. 20 of 1977 before the High Court Division which was also dismissed as not being pressed. The defendant No.1 then transferred 6.84 acres of land, as described in Schedule .1(Ka) to the plaint of Other Suit No. 53 of 1987, to the plaintiffs on the basis of "Angshanama" executed and registered on 18.3.1986 and delivered possession to them. Since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the said land. Thus the defendant No.1 was left with the remaining portion of land which he has been owning and possessing. But the defendant No.1 and other defendants on the basis of a created and collusive agreement/ solenama dated 18.5.1983, allegedly authenticated by swearing affidavit before the Notary public, claimed title in the suit land. The defendants disclosed about the said agreement/ solenama in their written statement filed in Other Suit No. 111 of 1984 instituted by Abul Kalam(defendant No.1 of other Class Suit No. 53 of 1988). But the said solenama was never acted upon and no possession was ever delivered on the basis of the same. The said agreement/solenama was created to get rid of a murder case. The same is a product of collusion and forgery and as such the same is void a initio. Such illegal claim of the defendants compelled the plaintiff to institute the instant Suit No. 53 of 1987. 

 6. The trial court, after hearing the parties, decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 8.11.1988 holding that the solenama dated 18.05.1983 is illegal, fraudulent, collusive, inoperative and by the same the title of the plaintiff in the suit land has not been affected. The trial court also passed a decree for permanent injunction as sought for. 

 11. Mr. Md. Delowar Hossain, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants submits that since the appellate court affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court, in all aspects it was not mandatory for the said court to discuss and consider each and every piece of evidence and each of the issues as well in view of the provisions of Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that the appellate court having concurred with the findings of the trial court as to the validity and genuineness of the impugned agreement/solenama and also having found possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land, the High Court Division committed an error of law in setting aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court and sending the appeal back on remand to the appellate court since, the High Court Division could easily dispose of the appeal on merit on the face of all the materials being available before it but without doing so, the High Court Division by sending the appeal back on remand actually has shirked its responsibilities and hence the same is liable to be set aside. 

 13. From a perusal of materials on record it appears that points raised for determination in this appeal are whether the appellate Court while affirming the judgment of the trial Court is legally bound to discuss and consider each and every piece of evidence and each issue as well on the face of Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code even if it concurred with the findings as to the validity of the agreement/ solenama and also as to the possession and accordingly whether the High Court Division erred in law in setting aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court and remanding the appeal to the Court of appeal below and whether the High Court Division ought to have dis-posed of the matter on merit since all the materials were available before it.
